What worries me more than the number is the sales cycle. It's gone from 41 days to 58 in two quarters, and nobody on the team can tell me why. That's the thing I'd like to spend October on.

This chapter reports the survey results (n = 212). The clearest split is by age: 68% of respondents aged 25-34 report daily use, against 31% of those over 55. That broadly matches Van Dijk (2019), though he used wider age bands, which makes direct comparison awkward.

One limitation is worth stating up front. The survey was distributed through university channels, so graduates are over-represented, and I return to what that does to the interpretation in section 5.3.

I think there should be more flowers along the roads.

Sixty-two percent of participants rated the programme as useful, down from 71% in the previous edition. One plausible explanation is that this year's cohort was more mixed: both new starters and very experienced staff took part, and both groups said the pace didn't suit them.

We recommend splitting intake into two levels next year and shortening the programme from ten weeks to six.
